steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with the molecules in Earth's atmosphere. Shorter wavelengths of light (blue and violet) are scattered much more strongly than longer wavelengths (red and orange), spreading blue light in all directions across the sky. Although violet light is scattered even more than blue, our eyes are more sensitive to blue light and some violet is absorbed in the upper atmosphere, so the sky ultimately appears blue to us.
